You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug reported is that when a parameter value starts with a hyphen (e.g., "-something"), the PosixParser misinterprets it as a new parameter rather than a value. The failing test has an array of arguments {"-t", "-something"} and it expects "-something" to be treated as a value for the option "-t", but it is instead recognized as a parameter, leading to misinterpretation.

From the code of PosixParser.parse(Options, String[], Properties, boolean), the parsing process starts by calling flatten() method which processes the command line arguments into tokens. The flatten() method iterates over the arguments and handles each token:

- If a token starts with "--", it splits it at '=' if any.
- If a token is a single "-", it calls processSingleHyphen.
- If a token starts with "-", for tokens of length 2 it calls processOptionToken, else it checks if the options has that token directly, and if not, it calls burstToken to split the token into multiple single-character options.

In the current bug context, the parameter value is "-something" which is longer than 2 characters and is not a registered option. So flatten() calls burstToken on "-something".

Looking at burstToken, it iterates through each character after the '-', checks if the character corresponds to an option, and adds it as a separate option, along with the remaining substring if the option has an argument.

This bursting of tokens treats "-something" as multiple options: "s", "o", "m", etc. This is incorrect because "-something" should be treated as a single value argument passed to some option, not multiple options.

Hence, the root cause is that burstToken logic handles unknown tokens starting with '-' and longer than 2 characters by splitting into individual option characters, instead of recognizing it as a value.

The flag stopAtNonOption is relevant to treat unknown tokens as values when true, but in the test case and PosixParser, this flag is false by default, so bursting occurs.

The problem occurs because the parser does not provide a way to tell that "-something" is not an option but a parameter value, and the flat tokenization and bursting logic mishandles this case. Possibly the code in flatten or burstToken needs to be adjusted to treat such tokens as values or the parser needs an option to stop option parsing for parameters starting with '-'.

No other recent bug reports directly relate to treating parameter values with leading hyphens, but one talks about allowing '-' in arguments (e.g., -Dnumber=-1) which seems related but not identical.

Summary: The bug is due to burstToken method splitting parameter values starting with '-' into multiple options because the parser treats unknown tokens starting with '-' and longer than 2 characters as multiple single-character options instead of single argument values.

Next, the best fix locations should be in the PosixParser flatten, burstToken methods and possibly in how stopAtNonOption flag is handled or exposed to users.
org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.flatten(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], boolean)
org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.burstToken(java.lang.String, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
